heading: Tender tip: partner to qualify
body: Lacking the grade, experience or capacity? A joint venture with a firm that has it can make you eligible. Agree terms early.

heading: Follow the format
body: Word limits, file types and page counts are rules. Break them and you can be disqualified.

heading: Tender tip: cross-reference everything
body: Build an index mapping each scored criterion to an exact page. Not cross-referenced often means not submitted.

heading: Investor tip: corporate VC wants fit
body: A corporate venture arm backs what fits its parent's business. Lead with that strategic fit, not only the return.

heading: Tender tip: watch for cure requests
body: After submitting, check the named contact email daily. Cure windows run from a day to a week, and missing one means disqualification.

heading: Reuse your best answers
body: Keep a library of your strongest paragraphs. Every new application gets faster.

heading: Tender tip: never inflate preference claims
body: A false preference-points claim can get you disqualified, blacklisted for up to ten years and referred for prosecution. Claim only what you can prove.

heading: Investor tip: know the funder type
body: Venture, private equity, corporate venture and government funds each want different things. Match your ask to the type before you write.

heading: Apply to more than one
body: Funding is a numbers game. Spread applications across grants, tenders and investors.

heading: Tender tip: choose firm or non-firm
body: If the method-of-pricing form offers firm or non-firm, select one. A blank option means your bid is not considered.

heading: Tender tip: B-BBEE, still submit
body: Missing B-BBEE proof usually costs points, not the bid, unless it sits in a pass/fail table. Check which table, then submit anyway.

heading: Fit the focus area plainly
body: Grants name a focus area. Apply only where your project sits squarely inside it; a stretch rarely scores.

heading: Tender tip: know the objection window
body: Awards can be challenged within a set period. Note the window in the pack so you can object if the process was unfair.

heading: Investor tip: know your numbers cold
body: Be ready to state monthly revenue, costs, cash left and growth rate from memory. Fumbling a number ends the meeting.

heading: Tender tip: read locality clauses
body: Locality can be a hard gate, a scored item or a deduction from every payment. Read for it and price it, not just score it.

heading: Grant, prize or programme
body: A third of listed calls are accelerators, challenges or awards, not grants. Check whether cash is guaranteed or only for one winner.

heading: Tender tip: keep a bid register
body: Log every bid: buyer, price, outcome and score. Over time it shows which buyers and price points you actually win.

heading: Confirm on the funder's page
body: Aggregator listings copy each other and go stale. Confirm the deadline and terms on the funder's own page before you start.

heading: Tender tip: use black ink
body: Use black non-erasable ink unless the pack says otherwise. Pencil or red ink can void the bid at many buyers.

heading: Investor tip: know your stage
body: Pitch investors who back your stage. A seed fund will not lead your Series B, and the reverse.

heading: Tender tip: get your COIDA letter
body: Works and site-based services usually need a COIDA Letter of Good Standing. No employees? Get a commissioned exemption affidavit instead.

heading: Check the country first
body: Most grants listed online are limited to another country. Confirm the funder accepts South African applicants before reading further.

heading: Tender tip: prepare for verification
body: Buyers may inspect premises, fleet and staff at short notice. A failed verification disqualifies; it does not just deduct.

heading: Tender tip: diarise certificate renewals
body: Note the expiry of every certificate in the bid. Validity often runs past closing, and a lapsed registration can invalidate the tender.

heading: Investor tip: reference-check investors
body: Ask founders they have backed, including ones that failed, how the investor behaved when things went wrong.

heading: Debt is also funding
body: Not every business should sell shares. With steady cash flow, a loan or asset finance can be cheaper than equity.

heading: Tender tip: panels are not revenue
body: Getting onto a panel buys the right to compete in mini-competitions, not orders. Budget your bid cost accordingly.

heading: Tender tip: register your own profile
body: On e-tender portals, register your own company profile well in advance and verify the submission status shows complete.

heading: Ring-fence grant money
body: Keep grant funds in a separate account or ledger. Funders and auditors will ask exactly where each rand went.

heading: Tender tip: talk only to SCM
body: Speak only to the named supply chain contact. Approaching other officials counts as trying to influence and can disqualify you.

heading: Investor tip: use their industry tag
body: Funders filter by industry tags such as fintech, health or agritech. Describe your business in the tag they use.

heading: Tender tip: warn your referees
body: Buyers do phone referees. Tell yours to expect a call and check their numbers still work.

heading: Plan inside the grant term
body: Grants often fund a fixed period, such as twelve months. Design a project that finishes and reports inside that window.

heading: Tender tip: late by a second
body: Proof of posting is not proof of delivery. Be in the box or showing complete on the portal before closing.

heading: Keep your books current
body: Up-to-date management accounts are the first thing funders and investors ask for. Stale books signal weak control.

heading: Tender tip: check subcontracting rules
body: Before designing delivery, check whether subcontracting is banned, consent-gated, capped or mandatory in this pack. Disclose every subcontractor.

heading: Investor tip: qualify the investor
body: Ask early whether they have money to deploy now and what cheque size they write. Save meetings for real prospects.

heading: Tender tip: rates clearance for directors
body: Municipal tenders want rates and taxes clearance for the company and every director. Start collecting director proofs on day one.

heading: Know your unit economics
body: Know what one customer costs to win and what they bring in. It is the first question a serious funder asks.

heading: Tender tip: watch the eTenders portal
body: National and provincial tenders are published on the government eTenders portal. Check it weekly for your category.

heading: Investor tip: address a named partner
body: Every funder card in the registry names a contact person and their LinkedIn page. Write to a named partner, not the general inbox.

heading: Tender tip: JV means signed agreement
body: A joint venture needs a signed JV agreement before submission. A letter of intent to sign later is rejected.

heading: Show you can deliver
body: Name your team and what they have done before. Funders back people as much as plans.

heading: Tender tip: win small quotes first
body: Below tender thresholds, buyers ask CSD suppliers for quotations. Winning small quotes builds the track record for big bids.

heading: Accelerators may take equity
body: Accelerator programmes sit beside grants in listings, but some take equity in return. Read the terms before counting it as free money.

heading: Tender tip: keep notes per buyer
body: Each buyer has habits: portal or box, cure windows or single-shot, what they reject. Keep a note per buyer and reuse it.

heading: Investor tip: match the territory
body: Funders list the countries and industries they back. Cross a fund off your list if South Africa is not on theirs.

heading: Tender tip: state employees cannot bid
body: If any director works for the state, get written approval for outside work first. Without it the bid is barred.

heading: Only chase grants that fit
body: Apply for grants that fund work you would do anyway. Bending the business to fit a grant costs more than it pays.

heading: Tender tip: don't pad or unbalance
body: Do not load contingency lines or unbalance rates. Both are rejection grounds, and conditional discounts are ignored.

heading: Tender tip: answer every disclosure question
body: Answer every question on the declaration of interest individually. One blank can invalidate the whole bid.

heading: Read the criteria first
body: Check you qualify before you write a word. Most rejections fail the eligibility check, not the idea.

heading: Investor tip: read the term sheet
body: Understand valuation, liquidation preference, board seats and vesting before you sign. Use a lawyer who has done startup deals.

heading: Tender tip: know the threshold
body: Where functionality is scored, find the minimum score on day one. Below it, your price envelope is never opened.

heading: Tender tip: spot award scams
body: A real award never asks you to pay a fee, buy from a named supplier or send a deposit. Verify with the buyer's SCM office.

heading: Check VAT on the amount
body: A few calls state the amount excluding VAT. Check which it is so your budget and the cap line up.

heading: Tender tip: lowest price takes all
body: The lowest responsive price gets full price points. Everyone else loses points in proportion to the gap, so know your points position first.

heading: Investor tip: tie money to milestones
body: Show what this round gets you to: the customers, product or revenue that unlocks the next one.

heading: Tender tip: no proof, no points
body: Every functionality claim needs the prescribed evidence attached and cross-referenced. Unsupported claims score zero, not partial credit.

heading: Get a second reader
body: Ask someone outside your business to read it. If they are confused, a reviewer will be too.

heading: Tender tip: register on CSD
body: South African government tenders need a Central Supplier Database number. Register before you bid.

heading: Ongoing means no deadline
body: Around four in ten listed calls are marked Ongoing. Rolling calls can close whenever the funder chooses, so apply when you are ready.

heading: Tender tip: check your tax status
body: Make sure your SARS tax status is compliant before the closing date, not after.

heading: Investor tip: no means not now
body: Investors rarely say no outright. Ask what would change their mind, then send an update when you get there.

heading: Tender tip: use the B-BBEE affidavit
body: Small businesses under the turnover threshold qualify with a sworn B-BBEE affidavit from a Commissioner of Oaths. No costly certificate needed.

heading: Ask within the band
body: Grant listings state a funding amount. Ask within that band; a request far above or below it signals poor fit.

heading: Tender tip: original tax clearance
body: Some buyers demand an original tax clearance certificate, not a certified copy. Check the returnable list and order it early.

heading: Tender tip: check the defaulters lists
body: Check National Treasury's Register for Tender Defaulters and List of Restricted Suppliers for your company and every director before you bid.

heading: Make impact measurable
body: Jobs created, people reached, revenue grown. Give a number and a date for each.

heading: Investor tip: name your competitors
body: Never say you have no competition. Name them and explain what you do differently.

heading: Tender tip: copies must match
body: Where both a hard copy and an upload are required, make them identical. Some buyers void mismatches; others let the hard copy rule.

heading: Record every small win
body: Pilot revenue, a signed letter of intent or a waiting list all count as proof. Log them as they happen.

heading: Tender tip: settle the VAT basis
body: Confirm in writing whether prices are VAT inclusive or exclusive before pricing. Some buyers deem large totals inclusive regardless of what you wrote.

heading: Tender tip: invoice exactly as told
body: Follow the buyer's invoice rules to the letter: order number, banking details, VAT number. A rejected invoice restarts the clock.

heading: Investor tip: run a process
body: Approach many investors in the same window. Parallel conversations create urgency; one at a time drags on for months.

heading: Count the days left
body: Before you start, check the days to deadline. If a strong application cannot be finished in time, save the effort for the next round.

heading: Tender tip: each JV partner complies
body: Every joint venture partner needs its own CSD registration, tax PIN and declaration forms. One partner's gap sinks the bid.

heading: Tender tip: arrive early at briefings
body: Lateness counts as absence at compulsory briefings. Arrive well before the start and sign the register in the bidding company's exact name.

heading: Lay out the logic
body: Put inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes on one page. Reviewers recognise the structure and score it faster.

heading: Tender tip: attend the briefing
body: Compulsory briefing sessions are compulsory. Miss one and your bid is out.

heading: Investor tip: set founder vesting
body: Vesting protects the company if a co-founder leaves. Set it up before investors ask, because they will.

heading: Tender tip: get it in writing
body: Verbal answers at briefings are not binding. Get every material clarification issued as a written addendum.

heading: Plan beyond the grant
body: Explain how the project keeps going after the money runs out.

heading: Tender tip: zero on one criterion
body: Some buyers disqualify for a zero on any single criterion even if you pass overall. Check for that wording separately.

heading: Convert to rand first
body: Most listed grants are in euros, dollars or pounds. Convert the amount to rand before deciding whether it is worth the work.

heading: Tender tip: no price in technical
body: In a two-envelope tender, sweep CVs and project descriptions for any price figure before sealing. One number disqualifies you.

heading: Investor tip: rehearse to time
body: Practise the pitch out loud until it fits the slot with room left for questions.

heading: Tender tip: include all costs
body: Delivery, travel, PPE, levies: anything not itemised in the schedule cannot be recovered later. Bake it all in.

heading: Operate where they say
body: Some funders require existing operations in named countries, not plans to expand there. Apply only where you already work.

heading: Tender tip: handwrite where demanded
body: Some packs require returnables completed by hand in black pen and reject digital completion. Check the pack's rule before typing.

heading: Investor tip: build a data room
body: Keep incorporation documents, shareholding, financials, contracts and key metrics in one shared folder before due diligence starts.

heading: Tender tip: disclose every linked company
body: List every CSD-registered company linked to any director, even ones unrelated to this bid. Hiding one leads to disqualification.

heading: One owner per application
body: Give one person ownership of each application, with a date for every section. Shared ownership means nobody finishes.

heading: Tender tip: keep CIDB grade active
body: Construction bids need the exact CIDB class and grade, active at closing. Read the eligibility clause: a few packs allow registration shortly after.

heading: Plain language wins
body: Short sentences, no jargon. Reviewers read hundreds of applications.

heading: Tender tip: initial every page
body: Where the pack says initial every page, do it, even for electronic submissions. Checklists audit this.

heading: Investor tip: ask for a number
body: Say exactly how much you are raising, what it buys and over what period. 'Whatever you can give' signals no plan.

heading: Tender tip: tick accept all
body: Where the contract conditions have an ACCEPT ALL tick-box, tick it. Leaving it blank is a disqualification on its own.

heading: Check state funders first
body: South Africa has public development funders and incentive schemes for small businesses. Check them before hunting abroad.

heading: Tender tip: return the addenda record
body: Sign and return the record of addenda with each addendum attached, and update your pricing where an addendum changes it.

heading: Tender tip: use free tender support
body: Public small-business support agencies offer free tender training and help with compliance documents. Use them before your next bid.

heading: Investor tip: short first email
body: Five lines: what you do, who pays, traction, what you are raising, and a link to the deck.

heading: Start early
body: Portals slow down on the last day. Aim to submit at least three days before the deadline.

heading: Tender tip: state the validity
body: Bid validity periods vary widely. If the pack states two different periods, price for the longer one and ask in writing.

heading: Tender tip: honour NO QUOTE blocks
body: Where the schedule says NO QUOTE, leave it. Pricing an item you were told not to price is also an error.

heading: Pool or per project
body: Read whether the amount is a total pool shared among winners or a figure per project. The two mean very different asks.

heading: Tender tip: label the envelope exactly
body: Endorse the sealed envelope exactly as prescribed, with the right number of copies. Defective labelling is itself a rejection ground.

heading: Investor tip: clean up ownership
body: Know who owns what before you pitch. Unclear founder equity or messy early deals scare investors away.

heading: Tender tip: keep CSD details current
body: Buyers source quotations straight from the CSD by commodity and location. Keep your commodities, address and bank details current.

heading: Keep one funding calendar
body: Track open calls, cut-offs and report dates in one place. A missed report can bar you from the next round.

heading: Tender tip: claim points in writing
body: Write the points you claim against each goal on the preference form and attach the named proof. Missing either scores zero.

heading: File receipts as you go
body: Grant spend must be evidenced. Save invoices and proof of payment when they happen, not at report time.

heading: Tender tip: sign everything
body: Unsigned SBD forms are one of the most common reasons bids fail. Sign and initial every page asked.

heading: Investor tip: compare the whole deal
body: A high valuation with harsh terms can cost more than a lower one with clean terms. Judge the package.

heading: Tender tip: assume no second chance
body: Smaller buyers are usually single-shot: everything must be in at closing. Bid as if there is no cure window.

heading: Apply as the right entity
body: Calls say who may apply: a registered company, a non-profit, or an individual. Applying as the wrong type is an instant no.

heading: Tender tip: file the attendance certificate
body: Get the Certificate of Attendance signed at the briefing and put it in the bid. It is a returnable document.

heading: Investor tip: start with angels
body: Angels and angel networks often write the first cheques before funds will. Begin there if you are pre-revenue.

heading: Tender tip: use the official forms
body: Never retype, reformat or substitute the issued forms, and never remove pages. Mark sections that do not apply N/A.

heading: Pick competitions by the judges
body: Pitch competitions bring visibility and sometimes cash. Enter the ones whose judges are funders you want to meet.

heading: Tender tip: never qualify your bid
body: Do not attach your own conditions to the offer or price. A qualified bid is non-responsive and cannot be fixed later.

heading: Answer the question asked
body: Use the funder's own headings and words. Reviewers score against their form, not your pitch deck.

heading: Tender tip: use the right channel
body: Submit only through the channel the pack prescribes. An email to a bid-box buyer, or a box drop for a portal buyer, is void.

heading: Investor tip: send monthly updates
body: A short monthly email to interested investors with metrics and asks keeps you in mind for the next round.

heading: Tender tip: price the spec exactly
body: Price the scope exactly as specified, not what you assume. A missed line in the spec means an unpriced or non-compliant item.

heading: Suppliers can fund you
body: Supplier credit and customer deposits are funding too. Negotiate them before you give away shares.

heading: Tender tip: register for RFIs
body: A request for information has no returnables, but register your interest anyway or you will miss addenda and the closed process that follows.

heading: Tender tip: attend optional briefings too
body: Non-compulsory briefings still reveal what the buyer cares about and who else is bidding. Go.

heading: Say what is new
body: Most listed calls fund innovation, technology or research. Say plainly what is new about your project, in one sentence.

heading: Investor tip: ask about follow-on
body: Some funds invest from seed through late stage and can follow on in later rounds. Ask a prospective lead whether they do.

heading: Tender tip: bidding costs money
body: Every bid costs days of work, certified copies and printing. Track your cost per bid and chase only tenders worth it.

heading: Tender tip: decide bid or no-bid
body: Score each tender on fit, capacity and chance of winning before you start. Bidding on everything burns money and staff time.

heading: Keep your documents ready
body: Company registration, tax clearance, B-BBEE certificate and bank letter: keep current copies in one folder.

heading: Tender tip: study past awards
body: Buyers publish who won and at what price. Check previous awards for the same service before setting your price.

heading: Investor tip: size the market bottom-up
body: Build your market size from customers and prices you can name, not a percentage of a global figure.

heading: Tender tip: never pay for influence
body: Paying anyone to 'assist' with an award is corruption and ends in blacklisting. Walk away from the offer.

heading: Name the risks yourself
body: List what could go wrong and what you will do about it. Reviewers trust applicants who see risks first.

heading: Tender tip: don't underprice to win
body: A price you cannot deliver on ends in penalties, termination and a poor-performance record that follows you. Price to survive.

heading: Prove the need
body: Back your problem with a real figure or source, not just your opinion.

heading: Tender tip: matched evidence sets
body: For each project claimed, attach the appointment letter, completion certificate and client reference together. One without the others scores zero.

heading: Investor tip: refresh your shortlist
body: Your fit with funders changes as you grow. Re-check industry, territory, funding type and stage whenever your business changes.

heading: Tender tip: points are not enough
body: Many buyers can pass over the top-ranked bidder for poor past performance or litigation against them. Keep your track record clean.

heading: Budget your own share
body: Some grants pay only a percentage of project costs. Check the co-funding rule and confirm you can cover the rest before applying.

heading: Tender tip: one bid per tender
body: Submit one bid per company per tender. A second bid, alone or through a JV, can void all your submissions.

heading: Separate business and personal money
body: Run the business from its own bank account. Mixed finances make due diligence painful and raise doubt.

heading: Tender tip: sign in ink
body: Sign in original ink unless the pack expressly allows electronic signatures.

heading: Investor tip: lead with traction
body: Customers, revenue and growth speak louder than the size of the market.

heading: Tender tip: budget for document fees
body: Some packs charge a document fee or need portal pre-registration before you can even download. Check access requirements first.

heading: Beware of fees
body: Real grants do not charge you to apply. Anyone asking for an upfront fee is a red flag.

heading: Tender tip: deliver, then get references
body: A finished contract with a happy client is your best bid document. Deliver well, then ask for the reference letter immediately.

heading: Tender tip: right CSD report
body: Check whether the pack wants the full CSD registration report or the summary, and how recent. Print the right one.

heading: Investor tip: follow up in writing
body: After every meeting, send a short note with the questions asked and your answers. Then ask for the next step.

heading: Match the funder
body: Read what they funded before. If your project looks like their past winners, say how.

heading: Tender tip: no Tipp-Ex, ever
body: Correct a mistake with a single line through it, rewrite beside it, and have every signatory initial it.

heading: Tender tip: certify copies fresh
body: Have company documents and director IDs certified by a Commissioner of Oaths from originals. Many buyers reject copies older than three months.

heading: Follow funders directly
body: Funders announce calls and cohorts on their own channels first. Follow them so you hear early.

heading: Tender tip: audit your financials early
body: Municipal tenders above R10 million need three years of audited financial statements. Unaudited accounts cannot be fixed in a bid window.

heading: Investor tip: warm intros work
body: An introduction from someone the investor trusts beats a cold email. Ask your network first.

heading: Tender tip: confirm the guarantee first
body: Before spending on the bid, check with your bank that you can raise the performance guarantee and absorb retention.

heading: Report on time, every time
body: Grant funders remember who delivers reports. A clean reporting record is your strongest case for renewal.

heading: Tender tip: fronting is a crime
body: Putting Black shareholders on paper only to score points is fronting, an offence under the B-BBEE Act. Real ownership only.

heading: Up to is a ceiling
body: An amount marked 'up to' is the maximum, not the typical award. Budget for less and justify every rand you ask for.

heading: Tender tip: vetting can override points
body: Some buyers vet staff and subcontractors after scoring and can disqualify regardless of points. Flag security-related tenders early.

heading: Investor tip: problem before product
body: Open the pitch with the customer's problem and who has it. The product comes second.

heading: Tender tip: reconcile the total
body: Carry the total from the pricing schedule to the cover form and Form of Offer in words and figures. A mismatch eliminates bids.

heading: Show who has the time
body: State who works on the project and for how many hours. Funders check that named people have capacity.

heading: Tender tip: return the POPIA form
body: Many packs include a POPIA consent form as a returnable. Sign and return it; omission is a missing-returnable kill.

heading: Investor tip: check the funding type
body: Funders state their instrument: equity, debt, grants or a blend. Ask for the type they actually offer.

heading: Tender tip: subcontractor compliance pack
body: Each subcontractor typically needs its own CSD registration, tax PIN, B-BBEE proof and company documents. Collect them before closing.

heading: Ask questions early
body: Most funders run info sessions or accept queries. Use them before the deadline, not on it.

heading: Tender tip: submit the escalation formula
body: On multi-year contracts, submit the escalation formula if one is offered. Omitting it usually locks you into fixed prices for the term.

heading: Cash or just support
body: Some programmes offer mentoring, networking and platform access, but no money. Decide whether that is what you need right now.

heading: Tender tip: plan for slow payment
body: Government pays on invoice after delivery, and often late. Make sure you can fund the work for months before money arrives.

heading: Investor tip: raise while you can
body: Start raising while you still have runway. A founder about to run out of cash has no negotiating power.

heading: Tender tip: claim every goal anyway
body: Ties go to the bidder with more preference points, then higher functionality. Claim every goal you can prove, even if price is your strength.

heading: Explain every budget line
body: Give each line a sentence: what it is, how you got the figure and why the project needs it.

heading: Tender tip: price every line
body: Leave no item on the pricing schedule blank. An incomplete price schedule can void the bid.

heading: Tender tip: references on client letterhead
body: Reference letters must be on the client's letterhead, signed, dated and with a contactable referee. Invoices and purchase orders are often rejected.

heading: Get letters of support
body: A letter from a customer, partner or municipality confirming your work carries weight. Ask early; they take time.

heading: Investor tip: check they still invest
body: Funds stop investing once fully deployed. Look for a recent deal before spending time on an approach.

heading: Tender tip: attach a board resolution
body: Prove the person signing has authority. Attach the board resolution naming them, or the bid is non-responsive.

heading: Tender tip: match every document
body: Names, ownership percentages and addresses must agree across CIPC, CSD, B-BBEE and the forms. Mismatches can zero your points.

heading: One page summary
body: If a reviewer reads only your first page, they should still know what you do, what you need and why it works.

heading: Tender tip: answer extension requests
body: Reply in writing to every bid-validity extension request before expiry. Silence can exclude you or lock you into a stale price.

heading: Investor tip: Global often means elsewhere
body: Many funds list Global as territory but are based in the US or UK. Check where their portfolio actually sits before pitching.

heading: Tender tip: rebuild the gate list
body: Universal gates stay the same; buyer-specific rules change every pack. Rebuild your gate register from scratch each time.

heading: Keep proof of submission
body: Save the confirmation email or reference number every time you apply.

heading: Tender tip: no alternative offers
body: Do not submit an alternative price basis unless the pack allows it, and then only alongside a fully compliant base offer.

heading: Find the partner first
body: Cross-border research calls often require partners in two or more member countries. Line up your partner before you start writing.

heading: Tender tip: sign the integrity pact
body: Where the pack includes a buyer-branded Integrity Pact or politically-exposed-persons declaration, sign and return it too. Omitting one can invalidate the bid.

heading: Investor tip: no deadline, no rush
body: Equity funders have no closing date. Build a shortlist and approach them on your timeline, not in a panic.

heading: Tender tip: build your own checklist
body: Sweep every page of the pack for anything to return. The pack's own checklist is often incomplete.

heading: Rejected? Ask why
body: Many funders give feedback if you ask. Use it to make the next application stronger.

heading: Tender tip: diarise the clarification cut-off
body: Buyers only have to answer questions lodged before the cut-off, which falls before closing. Find it on day one and send every question in writing.

heading: Investor tip: Africa funds skew early
body: Funders naming Africa as a territory are mostly seed and Series A venture firms. Raising later? Look beyond Africa-focused funds.

heading: Tender tip: start as a subcontractor
body: No track record yet? Subcontract to a winning bidder first. Their reference letters become your experience for the next bid.

heading: Show the numbers
body: Say exactly what the money buys: a line-item budget beats a round figure every time.

heading: Tender tip: confirm 80/20 or 90/10
body: Check the tender-specific clause for the preference system. Bids up to R50 million including tax use 80/20, above it 90/10.

heading: Promise what you can deliver
body: Targets you miss haunt the next application. Commit to what you can do, then beat it.

heading: Tender tip: read the contract first
body: The pack contains the contract you will sign. Read penalties, termination and payment clauses before pricing, not after award.

heading: Investor tip: understand convertible notes
body: Early rounds often use a convertible instrument that delays the valuation debate. Know the cap and discount before signing.

heading: Tender tip: nominate senior people
body: Score bands cliff on years since professional registration. Nominate your most senior registered people, with signed CVs and certified certificates.

heading: Budget must add up
body: Reviewers check the maths. Totals that do not match are an easy reason to say no.

heading: Tender tip: judge by content
body: An RFQ label can hide a full scored bid with a compulsory briefing. Classify the pack by what is inside, not the cover.
